motions.item_title: Adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming March 2025 as Multiple Sclerosis…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming March 2025 as Multiple Sclerosis (MS) Awareness Month. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: March named MS Awareness Month
motions.summary: The council proclaimed March 2025 as Multiple Sclerosis Awareness Month in Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: A ceremonial statement with no money or rules attached. Nothing changes for anyone in the city.

motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing items 12.A., 12.B., 12.C. and 13.C. from the agenda and moving them to the scheduled items. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Four items pulled for separate discussion
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after pulling four items out for full discussion later in the meeting.
motions.impact: Nothing was decided here beyond the order of business. The four pulled items got their own debate instead of passing in a batch.

motions.item_title: Table the Master Site Plan for Pinnacles B-3
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table the Master Site Plan for Pinnacles B-3. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Pinnacles B-3 site plan put on hold
motions.summary: The council set the master site plan for Pinnacles B-3 aside without deciding it.
motions.impact: Nothing is settled either way. The plan can come back to the council later. If you live near the Pinnacles area, this only delays the decision.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny the Preliminary Plat, Harmony 13. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Harmony 13 subdivision plan denied
motions.summary: The council rejected the preliminary plat, the proposed lot layout, for the Harmony 13 subdivision.
motions.impact: As drawn, Harmony 13 does not move forward. That touches the developer and neighbors near the site; the motion itself gives no reasons for the denial.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny the Harmony 14 Preliminary Plat. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Vote to deny the Harmony 14 subdivision plan
motions.summary: The council considered rejecting the preliminary plat, the proposed lot layout, for the Harmony 14 subdivision.
motions.impact: This is the step where the city signs off on how a subdivision is laid out, so it affects the Harmony 14 developer and anyone living near the site. The record here gives no reasons.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the First Amendment to the Eagle Quest East Master Development Agreement This item was discussed before Item 12.A.
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Resolution Approving the First Amendment to the Eagle Quest East Master Development Agreement. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Change to the Eagle Quest East development deal
motions.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the master development agreement covering the Eagle Quest East project.
motions.impact: The motion does not spell out what changed. A master development agreement sets the ground rules for how a project area gets built, so this matters mainly to the developer and to people living near Eagle Quest East.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement with the Valley Crossroads Chamber of Commerce for the ShopFestTM Utah event
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement with the Valley Crossroads Chamber of Commerce for the ShopFestTM Utah Event with the following changes: 1. In section five, changing the word “Chamber” to the word “City”, 2. In section ten, changing the term from five years to ten years, ending in 2035, 3. Add a “meet to confer” provision, 4. Change signature from Melissa Clark to Matt Everett, Chamber Treasurer, and 5. All future provisions for amendments to be in writing. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Ten-year deal for ShopFest Utah event
motions.summary: The city signed an agreement with the Valley Crossroads Chamber of Commerce to host the ShopFest Utah event, stretching the term to ten years, through 2035.
motions.impact: ShopFest is now locked in as a recurring local event through 2035. The rest of the changes are contract wording between the city and the chamber, and you will not notice them.
